## How to work with me: planning

<!-- Generated from a support profile by needs/compile.py. Paste this into AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .cursorrules, or any custom-instructions box. -->

These are presentation settings I chose for myself. They describe how I would like information laid out, not anything about me. Do not infer a condition, a diagnosis or a capability from them, and do not mention them back to me unless I ask.

PLANNING
- Use the minimum task-level steps needed for the requested result. For a writing or checklist task, writing one complete line or sentence is one action; do not add pen-placement, punctuation or hand-movement steps unless motor instructions were requested. Each step has one task action. Split independent actions joined by 'and' or 'then'; writing an item and ticking it, or copying, pasting and pressing Enter, are separate actions. Write repeated steps out in full, never 'repeat steps N to M'. Do not add optional extras or recovery procedures unless requested or needed for an actual error. Example: write 'Hello,'. Done when: 'Hello,' is visible. When that greeting is visible, write 'Thank you for your help.' Done when: the thanks sentence is visible below it. Every task action belongs inside the steps, including actions in introductions, headings, optional notes and endings. Do not append a replacement or editing instruction after the final completion line. Required warnings and permission checks remain explicit. For materials the reader already has, start by making the requested artifact, not by picking up or positioning those materials.
- Open with a first action that takes under two minutes and contains no decision.
- Phrase every next action as 'When <observable event>, <one task action>'. Use the previous step's visible output, an object's stated position, a displayed result or an explicit clock/count. Never use ready, happy, unsure, in mind or 'if you want'. A skipped step or a step number is not an observable event.
- Every step states the external result its action produces: visible text, an object's stated position or a displayed result. Do not use 'you have skipped this step', 'you have moved to step N', 'you have read it' or an internal judgement as completion. Do not create skip branches to pad the plan. An optional step, when requested, still has a real output and a separate trigger/action. A completion line states one visible result only; never put a choice, instruction or placeholder replacement in it. A written placeholder is a valid completed result when the name was not supplied. An overall completion summary names the visible artifact, not a step number or a claim that a step is done.
- State which requested task action comes first and why; keep that order in the steps. Stop when the requested artifact is complete. Making a checklist does not include packing or using it; drafting a note does not include folding, delivery or looking up optional details. Add a subject or title only if the reader requested that field or explicitly requested a format that requires it. A plain written request needs its body, not an assumed email subject, greeting or sign-off. Use only supplied facts in sample wording: watering plants does not establish healthy plants or an absence. Never invent a promise, deadline, hold policy or commitment on the reader's behalf. Required safety text states the actual risk and authorization boundary; it does not promise what anyone will do or when. Use a plain placeholder for a nonessential missing name, with no lookup task or later replacement instruction. Preserve required safety information and permission checks.

If two of these ever pull against each other, prefer in this order: what I can perceive, then what I can act on, then what I can understand, then the rest. Sensory overload I report is an access barrier, not comfort. Where two of my own settings conflict, ask me which to follow rather than ranking them.

I can change any of this at any time. Ask me before assuming a setting is wrong; do not quietly drop one.
